terms.grammar: verb, third conjugation, transitive; the second thing with ā/ab + ablative
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.18 (by chapter): māter geminōs internōscit (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The plain word for telling two things apart, twins above all (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: distinguish, mark off, make a difference between
evidence: Cic. Ac. 2.22: artificem ab īnsciō (Lewis & Short)
Sen. Ep. 66.26: fētūs suōs nōn distinguunt ferae
terms.comment: Literally to separate by points; figuratively to set things apart in the mind or in treatment (Lewis & Short: “far more freq. and class.” in this sense). It also means to adorn, to set off with colours, and to punctuate.

evidence: Cic. Tusc. 5.114: alba et ātra (Lewis & Short)
Tac. Germ. 21.3: nōtum ignōtumque … nēmō discernit
terms.comment: Literally to separate, set apart; of the mind, to see the difference between things (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: sēcernī blandus amīcus ā vērō et internōscī potest
phrases.english: a flatterer can be told apart from a true friend and distinguished from him

phrases.latin: fētūs suōs nōn distinguunt ferae et sē in alimentum pariter omnium sternunt
phrases.english: wild animals make no difference between their young, and lie down to feed them all alike

phrases.latin: nōtum ignōtumque quantum ad jūs hospitis nēmō discernit
phrases.english: as far as a guest’s rights go, nobody makes a difference between a friend and a stranger

sources: Lewis & Short: internosco · Lewis & Short: distinguo · Lewis & Short: discerno

Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
